body:
This morning, before I had even gotten to today's Gospel, my husband mentioned the women who followed Jesus. Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna. He wondered about them, and I told him to look into who they were.

Then I read today's Gospel.

There they were.

I had prayed before reading, asking God to give me some insight into what He wanted me to reflect upon today. So when I saw those same women named in Luke 8:1–3, I stopped.

Perhaps today I am simply supposed to notice them.

And so, in honor of my husband, I will.

Luke tells us that Jesus traveled "from one town and village to another," preaching the good news of the Kingdom of God. The Twelve accompanied Him, but then Luke tells us that there were women with Him as well.

And he gives us their names.

Mary, called Magdalene.

Joanna.

Susanna.

There are countless people who must have encountered Jesus during His earthly ministry whose names we will never know. Yet these women are named. Why?

Mary Magdalene had been healed by Jesus. Joanna was the wife of Chuza, a steward of Herod. Susanna is named, but Scripture tells us almost nothing else about her. Luke then tells us that these women, along with many others, provided for Jesus and the disciples out of their own resources.

I find that beautiful.

They weren't simply standing somewhere in a crowd listening to Jesus.

**They were walking with Him.**

They traveled the dusty roads. They moved from village to village. They gave what they had. They helped sustain the ministry that was carrying the Gospel into the world.

And perhaps that is exactly why Luke gives us their names.

Because following Christ isn't only found in the moments that everyone sees.

Sometimes discipleship looks like providing a meal. Giving money. Opening a home. Caring for someone. Walking beside another person. Staying when leaving would be easier. Quietly making it possible for someone else to do what God has asked of them.

And then there is Susanna.

We know almost nothing about her.

No great speech of hers is preserved. We don't know the details of her life, what she sacrificed, how long she followed Jesus, or what conversations she may have had with Him.

We simply know that **she was there.**

For some reason, that touches me.

We live in a world that often measures importance by recognition. We want to know whether what we do matters, whether anyone notices, whether our lives have accomplished enough.

Yet here is a woman about whom we know almost nothing, and nearly two thousand years later we are still saying her name.

**Susanna.**

God saw her.

Maybe that is enough.

Mary, Joanna and Susanna also remind us that the people who walk with Christ do not all come from the same place. They had different histories and circumstances. Mary had experienced profound healing. Joanna apparently lived within the household and political world surrounding Herod. Susanna's story remains largely hidden.

Different women. Different lives.

The same road behind Jesus.

Maybe that is part of what God wants us to understand.

We spend so much time wondering whether we are worthy enough, holy enough, knowledgeable enough, or important enough to be useful to God.

But Jesus simply says, **follow Me.**

Bring what you have.

Bring your resources.

Bring your wounds.

Bring your abilities.

Bring the life you actually have rather than the life you think you should have had.

And walk with Him.

Yesterday I found myself thinking deeply about my past, about forgiveness and about learning to love differently. Today the Gospel feels much quieter.

Today I see people walking.

Perhaps that is what comes after asking for mercy.

We get up and follow.

We don't have to know exactly where the road will lead. We don't have to become one of the people everyone remembers. We don't have to accomplish something enormous.

Maybe faithfulness is sometimes simply continuing to walk beside Christ and offering Him whatever we have available today.

Mary did.

Joanna did.

Susanna did.

And God remembered their names.
prayer: Jesus, thank You for the people whose quiet faithfulness has carried Your love into the world.  Thank You for Mary, Joanna, Susanna, and the many others whose names we may never know.  Teach me not to measure my life by recognition, accomplishments, or the mistakes of my past.  Show me what I have today that I can offer You.  And when I do not know what else to do, give me the grace simply to keep walking with You.  May my life, whether noticed by many or known only to You, help carry Your love somewhere it is needed.  Amen.
opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
title: Follow Me....
